To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1- nearest-neighbor (1-NN), random patient selection method, Cox-based regression method, and least absolute shrinkage operator (LASS0) methods were compared for predicting the survival of patients using the gene expression data of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA).

(1) the 1-neighborhood nearest neighbor (1- NN) method performed better than random patient selection in terms of survival prediction, even without a feature selection step and (2) using preexisting biological knowledge, such as gene pathways, may be a reasonable way to understand the biological systems of cancer, but not for the discovery of completely unknown genes relevant for cancer biology.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best survival prediction model is a Cox-based regression with nested cross-validation, using gene expression profiles from cancer pathways.
there are no universal methods to identify biomarkers for personalized medicine.
a feature selection method is not necessary when a large enough sample size is available, but it is necessary for smaller samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
using a small number of cancer pathway genes for survival prediction is a reasonable approach for cancer research.
a feature selection algorithm is not necessary when the goal of survival analysis is to predict the prognosis of a cancer, but is necessary when the goal is to identify biomarkers.
using a small number of genes for survival modeling is not necessarily inferior to using whole-genome data, if the genes selected are biologically relevant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 1- NN survival prediction method may be a good starting point for cancer survival modeling.
the optimal number of features for a given survival model is not a fixed number, but rather depends on the nature of the data and the analysis goal.
a combination of the 1- NN method and the Cox-based regression method may be a better approach to identify biomarkers for personalized medicine.
